{{Short description|Multilinear map that is 0 whenever arguments are linearly dependent}}

In [[mathematics]], more specifically in [[multilinear algebra]], an '''alternating multilinear map''' is a [[multilinear map]] with all arguments belonging to the same vector space (for example, a [[bilinear form]] or a [[multilinear form]]) that is zero whenever any pair of its arguments is equal.  This generalizes directly to a [[Module (mathematics)|module]] over a [[commutative ring]].

The notion of '''alternatization''' (or '''alternatisation''') is used to derive an alternating multilinear map from any multilinear map of which all arguments belong to the same space.

== Definition ==

Let <math>R</math> be a commutative ring and {{nowrap|<math>V</math>}}, <math>W</math> be modules over <math>R</math>. A multilinear map of the form <math>f: V^n \to W</math> is said to be '''alternating''' if it satisfies the following equivalent conditions:
# whenever there exists <math display=inline>1 \leq i \leq n-1</math> such that <math>x_i = x_{i+1}</math> then {{nowrap|<math>f(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = 0</math>}}.{{sfn|ps=|Lang|2002|pp=511–512}}{{sfn|ps=|Bourbaki|2007|loc=A III.80, §4}}
# whenever there exists <math display=inline>1 \leq i \neq j \leq n</math> such that <math>x_i = x_j</math> then {{nowrap|<math>f(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = 0</math>}}.{{sfn|ps=|Lang|2002|pp=511–512}}{{sfn|ps=|Dummit|Foote|2004|p=436}}

== Vector spaces ==

Let <math>V, W</math> be vector spaces over the same field. Then a multilinear map of the form <math>f: V^n \to W</math> is alternating if it satisfies the following condition:
* if <math>x_1,\ldots,x_n</math> are [[linearly dependent]] then {{nowrap|<math>f(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = 0</math>}}.

== Example ==

In a [[Lie algebra]], the [[Lie algebra|Lie bracket]] is an alternating bilinear map. 
The [[determinant]] of a matrix is a multilinear alternating map of the rows or columns of the matrix.

== Properties ==

If any component <math>x_i</math> of an alternating multilinear map is replaced by <math>x_i + c x_j</math> for any <math>j \neq i</math> and <math>c</math> in the base [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] {{nowrap|<math>R</math>}}, then the value of that map is not changed.{{sfn|ps=|Dummit|Foote|2004|p=436}}

Every alternating multilinear map is [[Antisymmetric map|antisymmetric]],{{sfn|ps=|Rotman|1995|p=235}} meaning that{{sfn|ps=|Lang|2002|pp=511–512}} 
<math display=block>f(\dots,x_i,x_{i+1},\dots)=-f(\dots,x_{i+1},x_i,\dots) \quad \text{ for any } 1 \leq i \leq n-1,</math>
or equivalently, 
<math display=block>f(x_{\sigma(1)},\dots,x_{\sigma(n)}) = (\sgn\sigma)f(x_1,\dots,x_n) \quad \text{ for any } \sigma\in \mathrm{S}_n,</math>
where <math>\mathrm{S}_n</math> denotes the [[permutation group]] of degree <math>n</math> and <math>\sgn\sigma</math> is the [[Parity of a permutation|sign]] of {{nowrap|<math>\sigma</math>}}.{{sfn|ps=|Tu|2011|p=23}}
If <math>n!</math> is a [[Unit (ring theory)|unit]] in the base ring {{nowrap|<math>R</math>}}, then every antisymmetric <math>n</math>-multilinear form is alternating.

== Alternatization ==

Given a multilinear map of the form <math>f : V^n \to W,</math> the alternating multilinear map <math>g : V^n \to W</math> defined by 
<math display=block>g(x_1, \ldots, x_n) \mathrel{:=} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \sgn(\sigma)f(x_{\sigma(1)}, \ldots, x_{\sigma(n)})</math>
is said to be the '''alternatization''' of {{nowrap|<math>f</math>}}.

'''Properties'''
* The alternatization of an <math>n</math>-multilinear alternating map is <math>n!</math> times itself.
* The alternatization of a [[Symmetric function|symmetric map]] is zero.
* The alternatization of a [[bilinear map]] is bilinear. Most notably, the alternatization of any [[Chain complex|cocycle]] is bilinear. This fact plays a crucial role in identifying the second [[Cohomology|cohomology group]] of a [[Lattice (group)|lattice]] with the [[Group (mathematics)|group]] of alternating [[bilinear form]]s on a lattice.
